# Hesaplamalı psikiyatri terimleri

URL: https://furkanbekdemir.com/notlar/terimler

Hesaplamalı psikiyatride ve hesaplamalı sinirbilimde kullandığım terimlerin
Türkçe karşılıkları ve her biri için karşılığın gerçekten yerleşik olup
olmadığı. Yetmiş terimin elli ikisinde o terimin Türkçe kullanıldığı bir
akademik kaynak bulabildim, on sekizinde bulamadım.

Bunu tezim için tuttum. Kendi metnimde aynı terime iki farklı karşılık
vermemek gerekiyordu, kararları da bir yere yazmam gerekiyordu, bu liste o
yerin kendisi. Bir standart önerme iddiam yok: yerleşik karşılık ilan etmek
benim yetkimde olan bir şey değil. Zaten çoğu satırda yaptığım şey karar vermek
değil, birinin çoktan verdiği kararı bulup kaydetmek.

Terimlerin bir kısmı psikiyatriden değil sinirbilimden geliyor. Çekici
dinamikler, Hopfield ağı ve enerji yüzeyi hesaplamalı sinirbilimin kelimeleri;
şizofreni modellerine oradan girmişler, Türkçeleri de o literatürde oturmuş.

Her satır ne önerdiğimi, neye dayandığımı ve dayanağın ne kadar sağlam
olduğunu söylüyor. Karşılığı olmayan terimi zorlamak yerine boş bırakmak,
listeyi kullanan birinin kendi kararını verebilmesi için gerekli.

kaynaklı · terimin Türkçe kullanıldığı bir akademik
kaynak var, ya da rakip bir özel anlamı olmayan şeffaf bir bileşik\
karşılık yok · yerleşik bir Türkçe karşılık
bulunamadı; ilk geçişte İngilizcesi verilmeli

Bir uyarı: `variational Bayes`, `generative model`, `hidden state`, `logit`,
`levels` ve `free energy` karşılıkları hakemli olmayan kaynaklara dayanıyor, bir
topluluk sözlüğüne ve bir popüler bilim çevirisine. Bunlar kaynaklı sayıldı ama
hakemli değil. `Laplace approximation` için bulunan kaynak Laplace
*dönüşümüne* ait; Bayesçi Laplace *yaklaşımı* ayrı bir şey ve Türkçesi yok.

Aramanın bir sınırı da şu: İngilizce arama motorları DergiPark ve TR Dizin gibi
Türkçe akademik veri tabanlarını zayıf indeksliyor. Her terim için ayrıca
hedefli tarama yaptım, ama bulunamadı demek yok demek değil.

## Doğru karşılık, aranan karşılık
Liste baştan beri tek bir soru soruyordu: karşılık Türkçe akademik yazıda
yerleşik mi. Sonradan ikinci bir soru çıktı ve cevabı çoğu zaman aynı değil,
çünkü yerleşik olmak ile aranıyor olmak ayrı şeyler.

11 Ağustos 2026'da birkaç terimi Google'da denedim. Ölçtüğüm şey arama hacmi
değil, motorun terimi tanıyıp tanımadığı. Google sorgudan kelime düşürüyorsa
("Eksik: ..." uyarısı) ve ilk sayfa bambaşka bir alandan geliyorsa, o karşılık
Türkçede aranmıyor demektir.

İkisi tanınıyor. `hesaplamalı psikiyatri` arandığında ilk sayfa çevrilmiş
yabancı literatür ve kurumsal içerikle doluyor, yani terim dolaşımda. `öngörücü
kodlama` da öyle. Buna karşılık `kestirimsel işlemleme` iş analitiğine kayıyor,
kestirimsel analiz ve kestirimci bakım içeriği getiriyor; bu listede o
karşılığın neden geçmediğinin ikinci bir gerekçesi.

İkisi tanınmıyor. `hiyerarşik Gauss filtresi` arandığında ilk sayfa görüntü
işleme oluyor ve yedi sonuçta "Eksik: hiyerarşik" uyarısı çıkıyor; kavramla
ilgili tek sonuç İngilizce. `duyusal azaltım` arandığında Google duyusal
yoksunluk ve duyu bütünleme içeriği getiriyor.

Aynı taramada `bayesçi beyin kuramı` sorgusunun gerçek bir karşılığı olduğu da
çıktı; ilk sayfada Türkçe nörobilim yazıları ve bir bilişsel bilim
topluluğunun sayfaları var.

İki şeyi ayrı tutmak gerekiyor. Bu, karşılığın yanlış olduğu anlamına gelmiyor.
"Duyusal azaltım" doğru bir karşılık; kimsenin aramaması terimin Türkçede henüz
dolaşıma girmemiş olmasından. Listenin işi doğru karşılığı kaydetmek, popüler
olanı seçmek değil. Bu satırlar da okura yazan biri için ek bilgi, çünkü ilk
geçişte İngilizcesini vermek aranmayan bir terimde aranandan daha gerekli
oluyor.

Ölçüm dört terimle sınırlı ve gizli sekmede yapılmadı, yani sonuçlar
kişiselleştirilmiş olabilir. Kalan altmış altı terim ölçülmedi. Ölçülmedi demek,
ölçüldü de bir şey çıkmadı demek değil.

## Model çerçevesi ve öğrenme kuramı
### Hierarchical Gaussian Filter
(HGF) · Hiyerarşik Gauss Filtresi · karşılık yok

Aradım, Türkçe akademik kaynakta geçmiyor. Model adı olduğu için İngilizcesini
ve kısaltmasını koruyorum; ilk geçişte "Hiyerarşik Gauss(sal) Filtre (HGF)" diye
açıyorum.

### Bayesian inference
Bayesçi çıkarım · kaynaklı

DergiPark'ta ve makine öğrenmesi kaynaklarında "Bayesçi çıkarım" olarak oturmuş.
Bazen "Bayesci" yazımıyla, ki bu bir imla tercihi, ayrı bir terim değil.

Kaynak: [Bayesçi Yaklaşım ile Regresyon Modellerinde Parametre Tahmini](https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/1688621)

### Bayesian belief updating
Bayesçi inanç güncelleme · kaynaklı

İki parçası da ayrı ayrı yerleşik ve Türkçe Bayesçi beyin yazılarında zaten yan
yana geçiyor. Birleştirmekte sakınca görmüyorum.

Kaynak: [Bayesçi Yaklaşım ile Regresyon Modellerinde Parametre Tahmini](https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/1688621)

### Variational Bayes
Değişimsel / varyasyonel Bayes · kaynaklı

"Değişimsel" bir topluluk sözlüğünde, "varyasyonel" ise günlük kullanımda. İkisi
arasında karar veremedim; kaynak hakemli olmadığı için ilk geçişte İngilizcesini
de veriyorum.

Kaynak: [deeplearningturkiye TR-YZ Terim Sözlüğü](https://github.com/deeplearningturkiye/turkce-yapay-zeka-terimleri/blob/master/turkce-ingilizce.md) (topluluk kaynağı, hakemli değil)

### Perceptual model
Algısal model · kaynaklı

"Algısal model" kendini açıklıyor ve başka bir alanda çakışan özel bir anlamı
yok. Çekinmeden kullanıyorum.

Kaynak: [Öngörücü İşleme ve Öngörü Hatası — Yayılmış Zihin (DergiPark)](https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/4835682), algısal/üretici model bağlamı

### Response / observation model
Yanıt / gözlem modeli · kaynaklı

Bunda da bir sorun çıkmıyor; iki kelime de tam karşılığı.

Kaynak: [Öngörücü İşleme ve Öngörü Hatası — Yayılmış Zihin (DergiPark)](https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/4835682), algı-eylem/gözlem modeli bağlamı

### Generative model
Üretici model · kaynaklı

Makine öğrenmesi kaynakları hem "üretici" hem "üretken" diyor. Ben "üretici"
tarafındayım, çünkü "üretken model" kulağa modelin çalışkan olduğunu söylüyormuş
gibi geliyor.

Kaynak: [deeplearningturkiye TR-YZ Terim Sözlüğü](https://github.com/deeplearningturkiye/turkce-yapay-zeka-terimleri/blob/master/turkce-ingilizce.md) (topluluk kaynağı, hakemli değil)

### Predictive coding
Öngörücü (kestirimci) kodlama · kaynaklı

Türkçede kullanılıyor ama tek bir hâkim karşılık yok: öngörücü, öngörülü,
yordayıcı, kestirimci, tahmine dayalı. Beş varyant saydım ve saymayı bıraktım.
"Öngörücü" diyorum, çünkü "öngörü hatası" ile aynı kökten gidiyor; ilk geçişte
İngilizcesini de veriyorum.

Kavram kaynağı (TR): [Öngörücü İşleme — Yayılmış Zihin (DergiPark)](https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/4835682); ayrıca [Öngörücü Kodlama ve Neokantçılık (Sabah Ülkesi)](https://www.sabahulkesi.com/2020/03/31/oengoeruecue-kodlama-ve-neokantcilik/)

### Prediction error
(PE) · Öngörü hatası (kestirim hatası) · kaynaklı

Türkçe Bayesçi beyin yazılarında "öngörü hatası" olarak yerleşmiş durumda.

Kaynak: [Öngörücü İşleme ve Öngörü Hatası — Yayılmış Zihin (DergiPark)](https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/4835682)

### Precision (inverse variance)
Hassasiyet / kesinlik (varyansın tersi) · kaynaklı

Ben "hassasiyet" diyorum, ama "kesinlik" de yaygın. Seçim keyfî değil:
"kesinlik" gündelik dilde doğruluk çağrıştırıyor, oysa kastedilen varyansın
tersi. Yine de literatürde ikisi de var, o yüzden ilk geçişte İngilizcesini
vermek gerekiyor. Bileşik terimde bulduğum Türkçe kaynak "kesinlik
ağırlıklandırma" diyor; kendi metnimde "hassasiyet-ağırlıklı" yazıyorum ve
farkı burada bırakıyorum.

İkisi de Türkçe kaynaklarda geçiyor.

Kaynak: [Öngörücü İşleme ve Öngörü Hatası — Yayılmış Zihin (DergiPark)](https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/4835682)

### Precision-weighted prediction error
Hassasiyet-ağırlıklı / kesinlik-ağırlıklı öngörü hatası ·
kaynaklı

İki parçası da yerleşik olduğu için bileşiği de sorun çıkarmıyor. Birleşik
terimin kendisi Türkçede yok, o yüzden ilk geçişte İngilizcesini veriyorum.

Kavram kaynağı (TR): [Öngörücü İşleme — Yayılmış Zihin (DergiPark)](https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/4835682) (öngörü hatası + kesinlik ağırlıklandırma; birleşik terim TR'de yok)

### Learning rate
Öğrenme oranı · kaynaklı

Makine öğrenmesi kaynaklarında "öğrenme oranı", bazen "öğrenme hızı". İkisi de
anlaşılıyor.

Kaynak: [YSA Eğitiminde Kullanılan Optimizasyon Yöntemleri (DergiPark)](https://dergipark.org.tr/en/download/article-file/1099311)

### Belief updating
İnanç güncelleme · kaynaklı

Psikoloji ve Bayesçi beyin yazılarında "inanç güncelleme" olarak kullanılıyor.

Kaynak: [Bayesçi Yaklaşım ile Regresyon Modellerinde Parametre Tahmini](https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/1688621)

### Volatility
Volatilite / oynaklık · kaynaklı

Finanstan ödünç alınmış. Borsa için oturmuş bir kelimeyi öğrenme kuramına
taşımak tuhaf, ama alan bunu çoktan yapmış; "volatilite" de "oynaklık" da
geçiyor.

Kaynak: [Enflasyon ve Enflasyon Belirsizliği: Türkiye Örneği (Sosyoekonomi)](https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/pub/sosyoekonomi/article/226831)

### Hidden (latent) state
Gizli (örtük/saklı) durum · kaynaklı

Topluluk sözlüğü latent için "saklı" ve "gizli" veriyor. Kaynak hakemli
olmadığından ilk geçişte İngilizcesini de veriyorum.

Kaynak: [deeplearningturkiye TR-YZ Terim Sözlüğü](https://github.com/deeplearningturkiye/turkce-yapay-zeka-terimleri/blob/master/turkce-ingilizce.md) (topluluk kaynağı, hakemli değil)

### Prior / Posterior
Önsel / Sonsal (prior/posterior) · kaynaklı

Bayesçi istatistik kaynaklarında "önsel" ve "sonsal" iyice oturmuş.

Kaynak: [Bayesçi Yaklaşım ile Regresyon Modellerinde Parametre Tahmini](https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/1688621)

### Logistic (sigmoid) function
Lojistik (sigmoid) fonksiyon · kaynaklı

Makine öğrenmesi kaynaklarında hem "lojistik" hem "sigmoid" geçiyor, çoğu zaman
aynı cümlede.

Kaynak: [Adaptif Sigmoid, Lojistik Sigmoid ve Tanjant Hiperbolik Aktivasyon Fonksiyonları (DergiPark)](https://dergipark.org.tr/en/download/article-file/2849675)

### Logit transform
Logit dönüşümü · kaynaklı

Pratikte "logit" olduğu gibi kalıyor. Topluluk sözlüğü "ters S" öneriyor; kullanan yok.

Kaynak: [deeplearningturkiye TR-YZ Terim Sözlüğü](https://github.com/deeplearningturkiye/turkce-yapay-zeka-terimleri/blob/master/turkce-ingilizce.md) (topluluk kaynağı, hakemli değil)

### Gaussian random walk
Gauss rastgele yürüyüş · kaynaklı

"Rastgele yürüyüş" zaman serisi ve finans yazılarında yerleşik, "Gauss"
niteleyicisini eklemek de sorun değil.

Kaynak: [Enflasyon ve Enflasyon Belirsizliği: Türkiye Örneği (Sosyoekonomi)](https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/pub/sosyoekonomi/article/226831), zaman serisi/finans: rastgele yürüyüş, otoregresif süreç

### Autoregressive process (AR(1))
(AR(1)) · Birinci derece otoregresif süreç · kaynaklı

Zaman serisi kaynaklarında "otoregresif süreç" ve AR(1) kısaltması standart.

Kaynak: [Enflasyon ve Enflasyon Belirsizliği: Türkiye Örneği (Sosyoekonomi)](https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/pub/sosyoekonomi/article/226831)

### Uncertainty (irreducible/estimation/volatility)
Belirsizlik · kaynaklı

"Belirsizlik" hem ölçümde hem istatistikte yaygın. Üç ayrı belirsizlik türünü
ayırt etmek gerektiğinde niteleyici eklemek şart, çünkü tek kelime hepsini
birden karşılıyor.

Kaynak: [Öngörücü İşleme ve Öngörü Hatası — Yayılmış Zihin (DergiPark)](https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/4835682)

## Model parametreleri
### Evolution rate
(ω (omega)) · Evrim oranı / gelişim hızı · karşılık yok

HGF'e özgü bir parametre, Türkçesi yok. "Evrim oranı" diyorum ama bunun yerleşik
olduğunu iddia etmiyorum, benim önerim.

### Belief instability
(κ₁ (kappa1)) · *(Adams'ın etiketi)* "inanç kararsızlığı" ·
karşılık yok

Adams'ın etiketi, Türkçesi yok. Ben bunu klinik ya da nedensel bir etiket olarak
kullanmıyorum; Adams'ın iddiasını aktarırken tırnak içinde ve ona atfen
veriyorum.

### Response stochasticity
(ζ / ν (zeta/nu)) · Yanıt stokastisitesi (yanıt gürültüsü) ·
karşılık yok

Türev bir terim, Türkçesi yok. "Yanıt stokastisitesi" ya da "yanıt gürültüsü";
ikincisi daha anlaşılır ama daha az teknik.

### Initial belief variance
(σ²₂(0)) · Başlangıç inanç varyansı · karşılık yok

HGF'e özgü, Türkçesi yok. "Başlangıç inanç varyansı" benim önerim.

### Disconfirmatory bias
(φ (phi)) · Çürütücü (yalanlayıcı) yanlılık · karşılık
yok

Adams'a özgü, Türkçesi yok. "Çürütücü yanlılık" diyorum; "yalanlayıcı" da olurdu.

### Belief / posterior mean
(μ (mu)) · İnanç / sonsal ortalama · kaynaklı

"Sonsal" yerleşik, "ortalama" zaten standart.

Kaynak: [Bayesçi Yaklaşım ile Regresyon Modellerinde Parametre Tahmini](https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/1688621)

### Levels (states x1, x2, x3)
Düzeyler (durumlar) · kaynaklı

"Düzey" ya da "durum", bağlama göre. Modelin katmanlarından söz ederken "düzey",
tek bir katmanın değerinden söz ederken "durum".

Kaynak: [deeplearningturkiye TR-YZ Terim Sözlüğü](https://github.com/deeplearningturkiye/turkce-yapay-zeka-terimleri/blob/master/turkce-ingilizce.md) (state="durum"; topluluk kaynağı)

### Scaling factor (sigmoid)
Ölçekleme faktörü · kaynaklı

"Ölçekleme faktörü" ya da "ölçekleme katsayısı".

Kaynak: [Adaptif Sigmoid, Lojistik Sigmoid ve Tanjant Hiperbolik Aktivasyon Fonksiyonları (DergiPark)](https://dergipark.org.tr/en/download/article-file/2849675), ölçekleme/ölçek katsayısı bağlamı

## Parametre kestirimi ve model uydurma
### Maximum-a-posteriori estimation
(MAP) · Maksimum sonsal kestirim · kaynaklı

Topluluk sözlüğü "en büyük sonsal" diyor, ama kısaltmayı koruyorum. MAP'i açık
yazmak kimseye yardım etmiyor.

Kaynak: [Bayesçi Yaklaşım ile Regresyon Modellerinde Parametre Tahmini](https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/1688621)

### Quasi-Newton optimization
Quasi-Newton optimizasyonu · kaynaklı

Türkçe optimizasyon derslerinde adı korunarak geçiyor.

Kaynak: [YSA Eğitiminde Kullanılan Optimizasyon Yöntemleri (DergiPark)](https://dergipark.org.tr/en/download/article-file/1099311)

### Multi-start (random restarts)
Çok-başlangıçlı optimizasyon · kaynaklı

"Çok başlangıçlı" ya da "rastgele yeniden başlatmalı"; ikisi de kendini açıklıyor.

Kaynak: [YSA Eğitiminde Kullanılan Optimizasyon Yöntemleri (DergiPark)](https://dergipark.org.tr/en/download/article-file/1099311)

### Log-model evidence
(LME) · Log-model kanıtı · kaynaklı

"Model kanıtı" yerleşik, "log" zaten öyle kalıyor, bileşiği de sorun çıkarmıyor.

Kaynak: [Model Seçim Kriterleri: AIC, BIC, ICOMP (İstatistik Araştırma Dergisi)](https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/pub/jsstr/article/1148498)

### Free energy
Serbest enerji · kaynaklı

Türkçede kullanılıyor, ama bulabildiğim tek kaynak popüler bilim çevirisi.
Friston'ın terimini hakemli Türkçe literatürde bulamamak şaşırtıcı değil, yine
de ilk geçişte İngilizcesini veriyorum.

Kaynak: [Bayesçi Beynin Geleceğinin Tarihi — Friston (CogIST)](https://medium.com/cogist/bayes%C3%A7i-beynin-gelece%C4%9Finin-tarihi-karl-j-friston-16dd2dc1d5a5) (popüler-bilim çevirisi, hakemli değil; TR akademik kaynak seyrek)

### Laplace approximation
Laplace yaklaşımı · kaynaklı

"Laplace" adı Türkçe derslerde yerleşik, ama bulduğum kaynak Laplace
*dönüşümüne* ait. Bayesçi Laplace *yaklaşımı* bambaşka bir şey; aynı adı taşıyor
olmaları kaynağı geçerli yapmıyor. İngilizce veriyorum.

Kaynak: [Laplace Dönüşümleri (Ankara Ü. Açık Ders)](https://acikders.ankara.edu.tr/mod/resource/view.php?id=54171). "Laplace" adı yerleşik; Bayesçi "Laplace yaklaşımı" özel anlamı için TR akademik seyrek, İngilizce verilmeli

### Parameter recovery
Parametre geri kazanımı · kaynaklı

"Parametre kestirimi" yerleşik. Simülasyon ve yeniden uydurma anlamında "geri
kazanım" diyorum, ilk geçişte İngilizcesiyle.

Kaynak: [Türev Tabanlı Parametre Kestirimi (ResearchGate)](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/349915965), "parametre kestirimi" yerleşik

### Identifiability
Tanımlanabilirlik / belirlenebilirlik · kaynaklı

Sistem tanımlamada "tanımlanabilirlik", istatistikte "belirlenebilirlik" olarak
geçiyor. İkisi de aynı şeyi kastediyor.

Kaynak: [Model Seçim Kriterleri: AIC, BIC, ICOMP (İstatistik Araştırma Dergisi)](https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/pub/jsstr/article/1148498), kestirilebilirlik/tanımlanabilirlik bağlamı; sistem tanımlama TR'de "tanımlanabilirlik"

### Parameter trade-off
Parametre ödünleşimi · kaynaklı

"Parametre ödünleşimi" şeffaf, yakın akrabası "yanlılık-varyans ikilemi" ise
Türkçede zaten yerleşik.

Kaynak: [Derin Sinir Ağları ile En İyi Modelin Belirlenmesi (DergiPark)](https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/821607)

### Prior distribution (mean/variance)
Önsel dağılım · kaynaklı

Bayesçi istatistik kaynaklarında "önsel dağılım" olarak standart.

Kaynak: [Bayesçi Yaklaşım ile Regresyon Modellerinde Parametre Tahmini](https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/1688621)

### Belief reset
İnanç sıfırlama · karşılık yok

Bu çalışmaya özgü bir işlem, Türkçesi doğal olarak yok. "İnanç sıfırlama" diyorum.

## Bayesçi model seçimi
### Bayesian model selection
(BMS) · Bayesçi model seçimi · kaynaklı

"Bayesçi model seçimi" sorunsuz, iki parçası da yerleşik. Ama alt terimleri öyle
değil, onları İngilizce vermek gerekiyor.

Kaynak: [Model Seçim Kriterleri: AIC, BIC, ICOMP (İstatistik Araştırma Dergisi)](https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/pub/jsstr/article/1148498)

### Random-effects BMS
Rastgele etkiler BMS · karşılık yok

Alt terim, Türkçesi yok. "Rastgele etkiler BMS" diyorum ve İngilizcesini de veriyorum.

En yakın TR bağlam: [Model Seçim Kriterleri: AIC/BIC (jsstr)](https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/pub/jsstr/article/1148498) (genel model seçimi; "rastgele etkiler BMS" alt-terimi TR'de yok)

### Protected exceedance probability
(PXP) · Korumalı aşım olasılığı · karşılık yok

Türev terim, Türkçesi yok. "Korumalı aşım olasılığı" benim önerim; kısaltmayı
koruyorum, çünkü PXP'yi Türkçe okumaya çalışan kimseyi görmedim.

En yakın TR bağlam: [Model Seçim Kriterleri: AIC/BIC (jsstr)](https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/pub/jsstr/article/1148498) (PXP alt-terimi TR'de yok)

### Exceedance probability
Aşım olasılığı · karşılık yok

Hesaplamalı model bağlamında Türkçe karşılık bulamadım. "Aşım olasılığı"
diyorum, ilk geçişte İngilizcesiyle.

En yakın TR bağlam: [Model Seçim Kriterleri: AIC/BIC (jsstr)](https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/pub/jsstr/article/1148498) (exceedance probability TR'de yok)

### Expected model frequency / model likelihood
Beklenen model frekansı / olabilirliği · kaynaklı

"Olabilirlik" yerleşik, "beklenen model frekansı" da kendini açıklıyor.

Kaynak: [Model Seçim Kriterleri: AIC, BIC, ICOMP (İstatistik Araştırma Dergisi)](https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/pub/jsstr/article/1148498)

### Bayesian omnibus risk
(BOR) · Bayesçi omnibus risk · karşılık yok

Türev terim, Türkçesi yok. Kısaltmayı koruyorum.

En yakın TR bağlam: [Model Seçim Kriterleri: AIC/BIC (jsstr)](https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/pub/jsstr/article/1148498) (BOR alt-terimi TR'de yok)

### Model evidence
Model kanıtı · kaynaklı

"Kanıt" ve "olabilirlik" ikisi de yerleşik; bileşik sorun çıkarmıyor.

Kaynak: [Model Seçim Kriterleri: AIC, BIC, ICOMP (İstatistik Araştırma Dergisi)](https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/pub/jsstr/article/1148498)

### Overfitting
**Aşırı öğrenme** (aşırı uyum) · kaynaklı

"Aşırı öğrenme" hâkim karşılık, "aşırı uyum" daha seyrek. Karşıtı "eksik
öğrenme", ki öğrenmeyi baştan bir erdem sanan birine ikisi de ters gelir.

Kaynak: [Derin Sinir Ağları ile En İyi Modelin Belirlenmesi (DergiPark)](https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/821607)

### Model space (factorial)
Model uzayı (faktöriyel) · kaynaklı

"Model uzayı" ve "faktöriyel" ikisi de doğrudan karşılık.

Kaynak: [Model Seçim Kriterleri: AIC, BIC, ICOMP (İstatistik Araştırma Dergisi)](https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/pub/jsstr/article/1148498)

### Winning model
Kazanan model · kaynaklı

"Kazanan model" tam karşılığı. Yarışma metaforu İngilizcede de rahatsız edici,
Türkçesi aynı rahatsızlığı sadakatle taşıyor.

Kaynak: [Model Seçim Kriterleri: AIC, BIC, ICOMP (İstatistik Araştırma Dergisi)](https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/pub/jsstr/article/1148498)

## Görev ve davranışsal ölçümler

ama adı verilmiyor, o yüzden ilk geçişte İngilizcesini veriyorum.

### Probability estimates (task version)

### Draws to decision

Türkçesi yok. "Karara kadar çekilen boncuk sayısı" diye betimliyorum, çünkü kısa
ve doğru bir karşılık bulamadım. Uzun, ama yanlış anlaşılmıyor.

Kavram kaynağı (TR): [Perseküsyon sanrılarını açıklamaya yönelik bilişsel modeller (Kriz Dergisi)](https://dergipark.org.tr/en/pub/kriz/issue/41029/495930)

### Jumping to conclusions

olarak yerleşmiş.

# Notes

URL: https://furkanbekdemir.com/notes

Explanatory notes on the methods the research pages depend on, written for
clinical readers rather than modellers. Each one covers what a measure does, and
where it stops being able to support the claim made from it.

Clinical readers · no equations · published

### [The Hierarchical Gaussian Filter, for clinical readers](notes/hierarchical-gaussian-filter.qmd)
What the parameters mean clinically, why model comparison is not optional, and
when a computational finding can be trusted. That a parameter can be estimated
does not show that it can be interpreted.

15 references · published

### [Sensory attenuation and the force-matching task](notes/sensory-attenuation.qmd)
Why self-produced touch feels weaker, how that becomes a number, and where the
mechanism has been found disturbed, from schizophrenia to functional movement
disorder. The task has two conditions and the measurement comes out of the
difference between them.

19 references · published

### [Belief updating in psychosis and hasty decisions](notes/belief-updating-in-psychosis.qmd)
How solid the jumping-to-conclusions evidence is, what computational modelling
changed, and why there is still no individual-level measure. The group
difference holds up; its link to delusion severity does not.

17 references · published

### [The Bayesian brain, prediction error and psychiatric symptoms](notes/prediction-error-and-precision.qmd)
What prediction error means, what precision sets, and why predictive coding can
be fitted to everything from psychosis to autism. Being able to fit that much is
also where the most serious objection to it comes from.

## Also in Turkish
These four notes exist in Turkish as well, at
[/notlar](notlar.qmd), alongside a seventy-term glossary of Turkish renderings
for computational psychiatry vocabulary. That glossary has no English
counterpart and is not planned to get one: its subject is which Turkish term is
established, which is not a question an English page can ask.

# Belief updating in psychosis and hasty decisions

URL: https://furkanbekdemir.com/notes/belief-updating-in-psychosis

In the clinic a delusion is described as a false belief held despite the
evidence, but that description stops at the outcome and says nothing about the
mechanism. The computational question is narrower: on the road from evidence to
belief, which step goes wrong?

This is my thesis topic, so I am writing as someone who both reads this
literature and is trying to get into it, and I have tried to keep apart the
places where the ground is solid from the places where it is not.

## The classic claim
Most of thirty years of literature rests on two jars and a handful of beads. One
jar is mostly black, the other mostly white. The experimenter draws one bead at
a time, and when the participant feels they have seen enough they say which jar
it is. The only thing measured is which bead the decision came at.

Deluded patients decide early. In Moritz and Woodward's sample, 42 per cent of
patients with schizophrenia named the jar after a single bead; in psychiatric
controls the figure was 7 per cent and in healthy participants zero. The finding
is called jumping to conclusions. A meta-analysis pooling fifty-five studies
points the same way: the psychosis group decides on significantly less
information (g = −0.53), and the odds of deciding extremely early run four to
six times higher.

## How solid is the evidence
The objection here is not to the group difference but to the sentence built on
top of it. To say "delusions come out of early decisions" you need early
decisions to track the severity of the delusion.

Ross and colleagues gathered individual participant data from 38 samples, 2237
people. The relationship is significant but small, r = −0.10. The subgroups say
more: it shows up in the 1754-person general population sample but not in the
262 people with current delusions, so the finding is weakest exactly where it
was built to apply.

An older meta-analysis tested four separate jumping-to-conclusions measures and
found only the bead count significant. In Lincoln's study of 71 patients and 68
controls the bead count was related to observer-rated delusion severity, but the
relationship lost significance once negative symptoms or IQ entered the
equation.

So there is no problem with the schizophrenia group separating from controls;
that patients with more severe delusions are hastier is a different claim
altogether, and we cannot say it has been shown.

## What early deciding is a sign of
Strube's comparison had 45 patients with schizophrenia, 45 with depression and
45 healthy controls. The schizophrenia group decided on fewer beads but took
longer to decide, and there was no relationship between decision time and bead
count either. Impulsivity does not explain this; the reason the authors point to
is instability in how the belief forms. Reasoning does not explain much either.
When Kemp and colleagues compared deluded patients with controls on three
separate logic tests, both groups made plenty of errors and the gap, in the
authors' own words, was surprisingly small; the deluded group endorsed more
fallacies only when the content was emotive, and they fell for the conjunction
fallacy less often than controls did. Sixteen patients and sixteen controls, so
a small study.

Balzan's group dug at another side of it and added an extra set of instructions
to the task. The over-adjustment seen when disconfirming evidence arrives
dropped markedly while early deciding did not change, which means part of a
finding that stood for years was the instructions not being written clearly
enough.

Speechley gathers the rest under one roof. Evidence that fits the hypothesis
gains more weight than it should in a deluded patient, while evidence that does
not fit stays at normal weight. The same asymmetry shows up as early deciding at
the start of the sequence and as over-adjustment in the middle of it.

## What modelling changed
The approach of the last decade has been to stop counting beads and model the
process behind the decision, which enriched the picture and disordered it.

The largest sample is Hauke's, 261 patients with psychosis and 56 controls.
Belief instability was high in patients, and jumping to conclusions was related
both to that and to the size of the initial uncertainty. The difference came out
between patients and controls, and between those who jumped and those who did
not; it did not come out between patients with few current delusions and
patients with many. The most interesting part of the same study clinically was
that belief instability predicted the response to metacognitive training at the
individual level.

Fromm's design deliberately separates diagnosis from symptom: healthy people
with few and with many delusional ideas, patients with few and with many.
Delusions were related to an increase in the precision-weighted prediction error
response in fronto-striatal regions; a schizophrenia diagnosis was related to
volatility being estimated higher than it is and to its neural representation
being weakened, so the two axes do not attach to the same parameter.

When Sheffield looked at paranoia, prior beliefs about volatility were related
to paranoia and not to unusual thought content or to anxiety. Sloan went a step
further back to childhood adversity and showed that adversity of the threat type
in particular was related to expecting higher volatility. Mikus drew the line
along the symptom axis instead; positive symptoms were related to uncertainty
about volatility, negative symptoms to rigid beliefs about observation noise.

## The same parameter turns up elsewhere
Estimating volatility high is read now and then as the signature of psychosis,
but that is a generous reading.

Gibbs-Dean's systematic review put psychosis, anxiety and depression in the same
frame; difficulty adapting to changing probabilities was there in psychosis and
in anxiety alike. As a doctor who sees anxious patients in the clinic I did not
find that surprising. My own published study pointed the same way: in
generalised anxiety disorder tonic volatility was higher than in controls and
was related to state anxiety. Thirty-six people, cross-sectional and
exploratory, so it does not carry much weight; the details are
[here](../research/anxiety-hgf.qmd).

Katthagen's review makes it harder still. There are studies relating psychosis
to too much updating and studies relating it to too little, and the variability
between tasks and samples is high; a parameter whose direction changes from
study to study is not one we can yet give the name of a mechanism.

## Formation or maintenance
Mashima's group split the beads task in two. The first stage is the classic
version, with beads drawn until the participant reaches a conclusion. In the
second, drawing continues and the participant decides whether to abandon the
conclusion they reached; on some trials the beads arriving contradict it.

The groups did not separate in the first stage. In the second, the schizophrenia
group wanted significantly more beads before abandoning the conclusion they had
reached, most of all in patients whose delusions were prominent. Twenty-nine
patients in a single study, so caution is in order, but the question it asks
holds up: the step that goes wrong may not be forming the belief but giving it
up, in which case the word to underline in the clinical definition of a delusion
would be irreversibility rather than haste. I write that as a possibility waiting
to be tested rather than as a claim.

## How reliable is the measurement
For a parameter to be of use in the clinic it is not enough that it separates
groups; it also has to come out similar when the same person is measured again
two weeks later.

Karvelis's group tried this. Thirty-nine healthy participants completed the same
task twice, two weeks apart, and the data were modelled with the HGF. Test-retest
reliability came out largely low and was no better than the behavioural measures;
the main source the authors single out is the measurement noise that parameter
recovery reveals. So a measure with face validity at the group level does not
carry the same thing at the individual level.

Hess's team put part of the problem down to the data itself. Most of these tasks
produce a binary response, and a binary response carries little information. A
setup that also brings response times into the model markedly improves how well
parameters and models can be told apart.

What identifiability and recovery are is set out in the [HGF
note](hierarchical-gaussian-filter.qmd). What it comes to here is that group-level
statements in this literature stand on much firmer ground than individual-level
ones, and that the two kinds of statement change places in the same paragraph
often enough.

## Reading a finding
I start by looking at the name of the task. The beads task, the fish task,
reversal learning and advice-taking tasks are used on the assumption that they
measure the same concept, when findings do not carry across from one to another
easily.

What comes next is finer. "This was high in schizophrenia" and "this was high in
delusions" are no longer the same sentence; given that Fromm's design showed the
two attach to separate parameters, without knowing which is being indexed you do
not know what the finding says.

The least discussed question is the last, whether the claim is built at the group
level or the individual level. Two schools can differ in average height without
that telling you which school the child in front of you attends; in the same way,
a parameter that separates groups but cannot be repeated in the same person
counts as a finding and not as a measure.

I will update this page as the thesis moves along. I expect some of what I have
written above to be contradicted by my own data, frankly.

Sheffield JM, Suthaharan P, Leptourgos P, Corlett PR. Belief updating and
paranoia in individuals with schizophrenia. *Biological Psychiatry: Cognitive
Neuroscience and Neuroimaging*. 2022;7(11):1149-1157.
doi:[10.1016/j.bpsc.2022.03.013](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bpsc.2022.03.013)

Sloan AF, Kittleson AR, Torregrossa LJ, et al. Belief updating, childhood

2025;51(3):646-657. doi:[10.1093/schbul/sbae057](https://doi.org/10.1093/schbul/sbae057)

doi:[10.1016/j.biopsych.2024.08.021](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.biopsych.2024.08.021)

# The Hierarchical Gaussian Filter, for clinical readers

URL: https://furkanbekdemir.com/notes/hierarchical-gaussian-filter

In a computational psychiatry paper you see the name of a model, a few Greek
letters under it, and a sentence saying some parameter was high in the patient
group. This note is about what that sentence says, and more to the point what it
does not say.

No equations. The aim is not for you to be able to build the model but to know
where to look when you read a claim that came out of someone else's. For a
reader after the mathematics and working code, [Perception, Beliefs, and the
Hierarchical Gaussian
Filter](https://metaduck.com/computational-psychiatry-afterburn-hierarchical-gaussian-filters/)
builds the model step by step with `pyhgf`; the side you will not find here is
there.

## The problem it solves
Imagine watching a patient learn something. Say they are learning which of two
boxes gives a reward more often. What you have is their responses trial by
trial: on this one they said A, on the next B, then A again.

What can you get out of that sequence? At the simplest you count how many times
they were right. But that number says nothing about how the learning happened.
Two patients can get the same number right having taken completely different
routes: one adapting fast to every new piece of evidence, the other changing
their mind late but changing it completely when they did.

The Hierarchical Gaussian Filter assumes there is a person learning behind that
sequence and tries to describe how they learn with a few numbers; what it models
is not the behaviour itself but the process that produces it.

## What the hierarchy means
The "hierarchical" in the model's name refers to layers of uncertainty sitting
on top of one another.

The bottom layer is the current state: is the box giving a reward right now. The
layer above it is the tendency behind that state: how often does this box give a
reward in general. The top layer is how volatile the world is, that is, how
often these rules change.

The model's real idea is in that third layer, and it is also the layer with the
most to say in the clinic. How fast you ought to learn depends on how much the
world is changing. If the rules change often it is sensible to adapt quickly to
new evidence; if the rules are fixed, the same speed sends you chasing noise.

People make this adjustment constantly, and the model puts a number on it.
Someone who takes the world to be more volatile than it is makes too much of a
single event, while someone who takes it the other way is slow to notice
something that really has changed.

## What the parameters say clinically
The number reported most often is the learning rate, and what is different about
the HGF here is that the rate is not fixed. In classical learning models a
person has one learning speed and it stays the same from trial to trial. In the
HGF it is worked out again on every trial, and according to how sure the person
is at that moment and how volatile they take the world to be. Learning speeds up
after a surprising event and slows down inside a familiar pattern.

The quantity that sets this is called precision. It has nothing to do with
precision in the everyday sense; it measures how narrow a belief is. A narrow
belief leaves little room for new evidence, a wide one leaves a lot. This is the
interesting part clinically, because the source of a symptom may not be the
evidence itself but the weight given to it.

The engine of the model is prediction error, the difference between what
happened and what was expected. But the raw difference is not what gets used;
the precision-weighted version is. A surprise of the same size has a different
result depending on how sure the person was at the time.

There is also response noise, the parameter that collects everything the model
cannot explain. A person may not act in line with their belief; they were
distracted, they hit the wrong key, they were undecided. Having this parameter
matters, because without it disorderly behaviour would look like a strange way
of learning.

The appeal of these numbers is obvious; each looks like a mechanism and attaches
easily to a clinical story. I wrote the two sections below largely against that
ease.

## Why model comparison is not optional
A model was fitted to the data and numbers came out. For those numbers to mean
anything you first have to know whether this model produced the data, or whether
another model could have produced the same data.

Goodness of fit does not answer that. A model flexible enough fits any data
well; a good fit may be showing you the model's flexibility rather than its
truth.

So building one model and reporting numbers does not count as enough. Several
candidate models are built, all fitted to the same data, and which of them
explains the data better is compared. Because the comparison also penalises
complex models, improving the fit by adding parameters is not an advantage.

If a paper has not done a model comparison, the parameters reported are not
showing a mechanism in the first place; they are the numbers you get when you
summarise the data according to that model. And the difference between the two
is not small at all.

## When to trust a finding
When a model fits data it produces a number for every parameter. That a number
was produced does not mean the data carry information about that parameter. In
some models two parameters move together: one goes up, the other goes down, and
the model produces the same behaviour. If you are filling a bath from two taps
you can tell the total from the water level but not how much came from which
tap. In a case like that the combination of the two can be read off the data but
neither can be read on its own. The estimation still gives you a number, because
it has to. And that number reflects the setup choices more than it reflects the
data.

The technical name for this is identifiability, and it is one of the first
questions to ask when reading a computational finding.

The way to test it is parameter recovery. You generate synthetic data with known
values, run the same pipeline on that synthetic data, and see whether the values
you put in come back out. If they do not, the parameter cannot be measured with
that design, and there is no way to work that out by looking at real data. I ran
this analysis on my own pipeline before collecting any data. I think the order
matters: leave it until afterwards and, when the result comes out badly, you
already have a number you could publish, and letting go of it gets harder.

Last, parameter names. Calling a parameter "belief instability" or "learning
flexibility" does not show that it measures that; the name is the interpretation
of whoever built the model, and the same number can be attached to a completely
different mechanism under another interpretation. Deciding between two
interpretations takes more than the model.

## In short
The clinical value of the HGF is that instead of treating learning speed as a
fixed trait, it handles it as a setting that depends on how volatile the person
takes the world to be.

But not every number it produces is a mechanism. The estimation gives you a
number under any conditions; what shows that the number measures something is
not the number itself but the model comparison and the recovery behind it.
Without both you have a summary statistic rather than a claim about a mechanism,
and if the parameter's name is bold enough, that summary statistic gets read as
a mechanism easily enough.

## References
The model itself:

Mathys C, Daunizeau J, Friston KJ, Stephan KE. A Bayesian foundation for
individual learning under uncertainty. *Frontiers in Human Neuroscience*.
2011;5:39. doi:[10.3389/fnhum.2011.00039](https://doi.org/10.3389/fnhum.2011.00039)

Mathys CD, Lomakina EI, Daunizeau J, Iglesias S, Brodersen KH, Friston KJ,
Stephan KE. Uncertainty in perception and the Hierarchical Gaussian Filter.
*Frontiers in Human Neuroscience*.
2014;8:825. doi:[10.3389/fnhum.2014.00825](https://doi.org/10.3389/fnhum.2014.00825)

Model comparison and parameter recovery:

Wilson RC, Collins AGE. Ten simple rules for the computational modeling of
behavioral data. *eLife*.
2019;8:e49547. doi:[10.7554/eLife.49547](https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.49547)

Rigoux L, Stephan KE, Friston KJ, Daunizeau J. Bayesian model selection for
group studies, revisited. *NeuroImage*. 2014;84:971-985.
doi:[10.1016/j.neuroimage.2013.08.065](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neuroimage.2013.08.065)

The software that implements it:

Frässle S, Aponte EA, Bollmann S, et al. TAPAS: an open-source software package
for translational neuromodeling and computational psychiatry. *Frontiers in
Psychiatry*. 2021;12:680811.
doi:[10.3389/fpsyt.2021.680811](https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyt.2021.680811)

# The Bayesian brain, prediction error and psychiatric symptoms

URL: https://furkanbekdemir.com/notes/prediction-error-and-precision

The brain does not wait for the incoming signal and then process it. It predicts
what is coming first and sends up only as much as the prediction got wrong. That
sentence became one of the most productive ideas in psychiatry of the last
twenty years, and the framework's most serious problem comes out of the same
sentence.

The other three notes rest on these two ideas without any of them setting them
out in full, so I wrote this one to close that gap.

## What prediction error means
The "error" here is not error in the everyday sense. Prediction error means the
difference between what happened and what was expected, and it is the only thing
the system uses to learn.

The appeal of the idea comes from its economy. If there is a clock ticking in
your house you do not hear it, and you notice the moment it stops. The sound
reaching your ear is the same in both cases; the only thing that changes is
whether it was expected. Most of the signal arriving from your sense organs
every second is like that, already what you expected. If instead of carrying all
of it upward you carry only the difference, most of the load going to the upper
layers falls away. Set out by Friston and Kiebel through the free energy
principle, the brain is a hierarchy of estimates: each layer tells the one below
what to expect, and the one below sends back only the margin by which it was
wrong. The collective name for the framework is the Bayesian brain; the name
given to its neural implementation is predictive coding.

What follows from this runs against intuition. Perception is not something
flowing from outside in but a hypothesis built from the inside out and tested
against sensory data. Clark's review presents this as a model that gathers
perception and action under one roof, and most of its popularity comes from that
gathering power.

## What precision means
This is where the framework is actually of use clinically, and it is also the
part most popular accounts skip.

If the pharmacy scale shows you two hundred grams heavier, that is information.
If you see the same two hundred grams on a bathroom scale that gives a different
number every time you step on it, it means nothing. The difference is the same
difference in both cases; what changes is how seriously you take the instrument.
The brain has to make the same distinction, and it does so by giving every
signal a weight. The name of that weight is precision: how narrow an estimate
is, which is to say the inverse of its variance. What goes up is not the raw
prediction error but its precision-weighted version.

Feldman and Friston went a step further and defined attention as that weight
itself. To attend to something is to raise the precision of that channel. Seen
this way attention stops being a separate faculty and becomes a setting of the
inference.

There is also this. What has been proposed as the neural counterpart of
precision is the postsynaptic gain of cells carrying prediction error; that
proposal ties the framework to neuromodulation, and that is where it really gets
into psychiatry.

## Precision at which level
Because there is a hierarchy there is no single setting. The precision of
sensory evidence and the precision of prior belief stand separately, and
symptoms are tied to the ratio between them.

The proposal put forward in 2013 and still treated as a reference is Adams's:
psychotic symptoms may be different faces of one core pathology, which is the
faulty encoding of precision. Hallucinations, eye movement abnormalities, loss
of sensory attenuation and delusions are all derived from that one framework.
Where sensory attenuation sits in this picture is in [a separate
note](sensory-attenuation.qmd).

## Which direction in psychosis
On the canonical account, the precision of prior belief falls relative to
sensory data in psychosis, the world becomes unpredictable, and a delusion is
the story built to explain that experience.

The findings are not that orderly. Sterzer's review says so directly; some
studies find prior beliefs weakened in psychosis, others find them strengthened.
Haarsma's group showed that precision-weighting of prediction errors helps
learning in healthy people and that this is disrupted in first-episode
psychosis. On top of that, they showed it can be moved with a dopaminergic
intervention. Corlett, updating the ketamine model, accepts that there may be
more than one route.

A single study can hold both directions at once. In Benrimoh's conditioned
hallucination study, people high in hallucination proneness both give more
weight to prior belief and come out with low sensory precision. In Goodwin's
two large-sample study, psychosis-like experiences went with giving too much
weight to sensory information, which is the opposite of the canonical account.

Sterzer's review makes its own proposal, which is to put the two findings on
different floors of the same hierarchy. When the prior belief at the lower level
weakens, unfiltered prediction error climbs, and the beliefs at the upper level
stiffen to explain the excess away; so weak and strong priors can be present in
the same patient at once. Because upper association cortex carries denser
recurrent connections than lower sensory areas, a disturbance in the
excitation-inhibition balance would also be expected to hit the upper floors
harder. Benrimoh finding both directions in one study fits this reading.

But this is a reconciliation rather than a tested finding. A study that does not
say which level its task measures can neither support nor refute the
distinction, and most studies in the literature do not say.

## The same framework explains autism too
Van de Cruys ties autism to prediction errors being given high weight
inflexibly. Every deviation in the world carries news. None of it can be written
off as noise. Findings about executive function and theory of mind come out as
secondary consequences of this.

Note that this is the exact opposite of what is proposed for psychosis; the same
framework and the same two parameters, run in the other direction. Friston,
Lawson and Frith argued separately about what to call this and proposed reading
autism as a disturbance in beliefs about precision rather than as a weakening of
prior beliefs.

Recent tests muddy this too. Arthur and colleagues, modelling two sensorimotor
tasks, found no lasting deviation in prior beliefs or in sensory weighting in
autism; what they found was difficulty flexing the learning rate according to
volatility.

## Body and emotion
The fastest-growing arm of the framework looks inward rather than outward. As
Seth and Friston set it up, bodily states are governed by estimation too, and
emotion is a product of that process.

Smith's team tested this in a transdiagnostic sample. In a heartbeat task, when
the bodily signal was disturbed by breath-holding, healthy participants raised
the precision they gave the signal from the heart, while the anxiety,
depression, substance use and eating disorder groups did not. No strong
difference was found in prior beliefs, so what separated the groups was not the
belief itself but the ability to adjust the weight.

## The framework's biggest problem
What has been listed so far can be read as the framework's success, but the
field has for some time been thinking the opposite.

Qela's review, covering seventy-two studies, finds something in every disorder,
but the things found do not resemble each other. Mancini and Nour put it in a
single sentence, that a model with this many moving parts is hard to pin down
anywhere. Alotaibi's 2026 review asks it in the title, whether predictive coding
is a mechanistic model or a metaphorical re-description.

A framework being able to hold both a finding and its opposite usually gets
called flexibility, but looked at from the side of testability it is hard to
call it that.

This is not a reason to drop the framework. As a doctor using it in my own work,
what I would say is that the sentence "precision is disturbed in psychosis" says
nothing on its own. Without answers to at which level, in which direction, on
which task and with which symptom, the sentence fits the framework but is not
tested. When a computational finding can answer those is in the [HGF
note](hierarchical-gaussian-filter.qmd); the same problem in the schizophrenia
literature is in the [belief updating note](belief-updating-in-psychosis.qmd).

# Sensory attenuation and the force-matching task

URL: https://furkanbekdemir.com/notes/sensory-attenuation

You cannot tickle yourself. Behind that familiar observation there is a
mechanism the laboratory can turn into a number, and where that mechanism
weakens, psychiatric symptoms appear.

Tickling is the most familiar form of it but not the whole of it. I am a
psychiatry resident and I work on this measure through my thesis, so what
follows is both what the literature says and what I learned building the rig
myself. The precision language used here is set out at more length in the [HGF
note](hierarchical-gaussian-filter.qmd); the rig itself is on the [instrument
page](../tools/force-matching.qmd).

## Why your own touch is different
There is no physical difference between touching your own palm and having
someone else touch it the same way. The pressure, the skin and the receptors are
the same. The only thing that changes is where the touch came from, and that is
exactly what lowers the perceived intensity.

Blakemore and colleagues looked at this in 1998. Somatosensory cortex was more
active for externally produced touch and less active for self-produced touch. In
the cerebellum the pattern reversed: cerebellar activity was lower for movements
that produced a touch than for movements that did not. The reading is that
the cerebellum works out the sensory consequence of a movement in advance and
that this is used to turn the incoming signal down. I say reading because the
study does not show that directly; it is only the simplest account that fits
what was found.

The name for that turning down is sensory attenuation. To see what it is for it
helps to remember that most of the signal reaching your senses is produced by
your own movements. If all of it were processed at equal weight, the externally
caused signal, the one that actually carries news, would be lost inside it.
Noise-cancelling headphones do much the same thing, predicting the incoming
sound and generating its inverse, so that only what they could not predict is
left.

## How the task turns it into a number
The most memorable demonstration involved two people. In 2003 Shergill and
colleagues had participants take turns pressing on each other's finger, each
trying to apply the force they had just felt, and the force grew every turn.
Nobody was exaggerating, everyone matched what they felt, but because they felt
their own output as weaker than it was, each put in a little more. The paper's
title sums it up as two eyes for an eye. Which means the line we all used as
children, that he hit first and he hit harder, turns out to have been a
calibration problem rather than a lie.

The same effect was turned into a standard single-person task. In the
force-matching task a target force is applied to the participant's finger and
they are then asked to reproduce it two ways. In the direct condition they press
on their own finger with the other hand. In the slider condition a motor
produces the force and the participant sets its size with a slider.

Pressing directly they overshoot, and through the slider they are fairly
accurate. In the twenty-five-participant data published in McNaughton's device
paper the direct condition ran 0.50 N high on average and the slider condition
0.30 N low, and the difference between the two conditions is what the
measurement is.

## What the slider condition is for
Why the slider condition is needed is not obvious at first, and misreading the
task usually starts from there, so it is worth slowing down here.

The error in the direct condition has more than one source. You have to remember
the target force, you have to scale the force you produce, and on top of that
your motor output has noise of its own. None of these is specific to prediction,
and each produces a deviation on its own. The slider condition carries the same
memory and scaling load, but because the force does not come from your own hand
the prediction-based part is not engaged. Taking the difference between the two
conditions cancels the shared effects and leaves the share that belongs to
prediction.

This logic was tested formally not long ago. Valè and colleagues built a
computational model of the task on data from close to five hundred participants,
separated the noise sources including memory noise, and showed that the
difference between the two conditions does isolate the predictive component. Two
more things came out of the same study. Attenuated sensations are more variable
trial to trial, because they carry the noise of the prediction as well. And
attenuation works by division rather than subtraction: a fixed amount is not
taken off the signal, the signal is scaled down by a factor.

What the attenuation locks onto has been tested too. Bays and colleagues showed
that the mechanism is tied not to the movement itself but to the event the
movement is expected to produce. Shifting the timing of the touch forward or
back reduces attenuation, and movements that stop above the finger or pass
beside it produce none at all. So the system is not saying "I am moving, turn
the sensation down" so much as "a touch of this kind is about to happen here,
now". Kilteni and Ehrsson showed a more basic condition on top of that: you have to
count the touching hand as your own. When ownership is shifted with the rubber
hand illusion, the attenuation shifts with it.

## The link to precision
In the active inference framework, attenuation means lowering the precision of
sensory evidence during movement. The argument for calling it necessary is that
in order to move, the prediction that you are moving has to override the sensory
evidence saying you have not moved yet.
If the weight of that evidence is not lowered, the movement does not start.

Brown and colleagues reproduced the force-matching finding from this framework.
When they removed attenuation from the model the overshoot in the task
disappeared and false inferences about agency appeared. So the same setting both
makes movement possible and determines what counts as yours, and it costs you in
both directions: lower it too little and the movement does not start, lower it
too much and you cannot tell yourself from the world. Let me flag one thing
here. This comes out of a model and depends on what that model assumes; it is
not something an experiment has shown directly.

## Where it sits clinically
One of the oldest findings here still says the most. In 2000 Blakemore and
colleagues compared patients with schizophrenia, patients with bipolar disorder
and depression, and healthy controls. What determined the loss of attenuation
was the symptom rather than the diagnosis: it was absent in those with auditory
hallucinations or passivity experiences, and present in those without them
regardless of diagnosis.

What followed widened this. Attenuation was shown to be significantly reduced in
schizophrenia; in the imaging study, the loss of attenuation in secondary
somatosensory cortex tracked the patient's hallucination severity at the time.
Teufel and colleagues worked with healthy participants instead: those higher in
delusional ideation were more accurate on the task, meaning they attenuated
less. That last one answers two objections at once, because neither medication nor
an active episode can explain it.

It would be a mistake to stop at schizophrenia. In functional movement
disorder attenuation is absent; patients do not feel the movement as under their
own control and do not produce the overshoot controls produce. In Parkinson's
disease attenuation is selectively impaired in the group reporting fatigue and
not in the group without it, and the impairment tracks subjective fatigue and
perceived effort rather than motor symptom severity. In chronic pain no group
difference in magnitude was found; what separated the groups was variance.

That the impairment turns up across such different clinical pictures already
makes this a measure tied to a symptom rather than to a diagnosis. It does not
tell you which diagnosis a patient carries, it says something about which
mechanism is disturbed, and mixing the two up promises more than the measure can
give.
I am not claiming it has a use in the clinic today; these are group-level
differences and they do not tell you what to do in front of one patient.

## What the instrument contributes
Because the measurement is the difference between two conditions, any instrument
error that is the same in both conditions drops out of the difference. The error
that does not drop out is the one that depends on loading direction, since the
two conditions do not load the sensor the same way. A ramp pressed by a motor
and a ramp pressed by a person are not the same thing.

When I built my own rig, the item that passed its acceptance criterion by the
narrowest margin was hysteresis, and that is not a coincidence, because
hysteresis falls into exactly the class of error that does not cancel in the
difference. The rig itself and the calibration records are on the [instrument
page](../tools/force-matching.qmd).

## Reading a finding
The first thing to look at in a published attenuation finding is how many
conditions the design had. A deviation coming out of a single-condition design
cannot be called attenuation, because what strips out memory and scaling is the
second condition itself.

Then come the repetition count and the time window. In data from a hundred and
thirty-eight participants McNaughton and colleagues showed three things. The
number of repetitions can be brought down from eight, the best window for
extracting the matched force falls between 2.5 and 3.0 seconds, and performance
does not drift over the course of the experiment. If the choice of window is not
reported there is no way to compare two studies.

Last, whether the analysis looked only at the mean. In chronic pain the groups
did not separate in magnitude but did separate in variance, and an analysis
looking at the mean would never see a difference of that kind. Given that Valè
and colleagues' model says variability may be signal belonging to the prediction
rather than noise, it is hard to call this a small detail any more.

I will update this page as I collect my own data, particularly wherever what I
have written here turns out to be wrong.
